source.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream
source.authors: A. Shai; Sarah E. Marzen; Lucas Teixeira; Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel; P. Riechers

page_placements.theme: Where features useless for the next token come from: retention for later positions vs circuit sharing

record.tranche_reason: The study conceptually tests whether predictive information beyond the next token is represented in transformer activations, using linear regression to recover ground-truth belief-state geometry rather than directly decoding future tokens.
record.gate_note: The study measures belief-state geometry and its relation to next-token predictions. It does not test rhyme generation, causal changes to intermediate text, or whether such representations steer generation. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Trains small transformers on synthetic HMM data and linearly decodes belief states from residual activations at one position. A belief state fixes the distribution over all future tokens, so this bears on V2 (future information in hidden states) in a new synthetic setting. It does not decode specific future tokens, and V2 is never named as a target.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude belief-state geometry, including fractal geometry, is linearly represented in the residual stream, sometimes only across layers, and carries information about the entire future beyond next-token prediction. They state they did not test whether it implements Bayesian updating.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear regression to recover known belief states from residual activations, rather than decoding future tokens from a hidden state or intervening on candidate future tokens and measuring generation.
record.method_sensitivity: The location of the representation differed by process: Mess3 geometry appeared in individual layers through the final layer, while RRXOR geometry was found only in concatenated activations across layers. Mess3 geometry was qualitatively similar before and after final layer normalization; the reported mean squared errors were 0.0004 before and 0.0003 after.

fits_no_version.finding: RRXOR belief distinctions with identical next-token predictions are retained across layers at each position. The authors argue this is needed for correct predictions at later positions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Next-token-trained transformers retain information that matters only for later positions, distributed across layers rather than in the final layer.

record.problems: Experiments use small synthetic HMMs with 3–5 hidden states and vocabularies of 2–3 tokens. The study does not directly decode future tokens, test natural-language models, or intervene to determine whether the represented information causally shapes generation. Some results are described qualitatively or shown in figures without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: Direct decoding of specific tokens several positions ahead; natural-language or pretrained models; accuracy at each future offset.
No test of whether features are computed for later positions rather than as a side effect. The authors argue it theoretically (Section 4.1) but do not test it causally.
Not tested. Board games and RNNs are only discussed or cited.

missing.what: Mess3 belief geometry is well represented in individual layers and persists to the final layer (per-layer MSE).
Lower belief-regression MSE correlates with validation loss closer to optimal, for both processes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'challenges' label on R5 is too strong. The beyond-next-token information is present at the position, but distributed across layers, so 'limits_scope' fits better. Future Lens (an original source) is cited only as consistent with this work. The setting is tiny: 3–5 hidden states, 2–3 token vocabularies, context length 10.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representations before a line and interventions changing the line to fit a different ending.

The study probes belief-state geometry as a proxy for information about future tokens; it does not directly decode tokens several positions ahead from a hidden state. Experiments use small synthetic HMM processes, not natural-language or frontier models.
No causal test of whether features are computed because they help later positions rather than as a side effect of next-token prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in open-weight models or with open attribution-graph or probing tools.
No experiments on multi-step reasoning, chess, Sokoban, or other architectures; these are discussed as possible applications or future work.
No test of planning depth, heuristic explanations of apparent plans, or whether a plan causally steers generation.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the Mess3 Process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Linear regression from final-layer residual activations to ground-truth belief states

conditions.value: final residual stream, before layer norm and unembedding

rows.measure: Recovery of the ground-truth belief-state geometry
rows.value: The projected geometry closely resembled the predicted fractal structure.
rows.note: The study describes the 2D subspace as a linear representation of the belief-state geometry; it does not directly decode future tokens.
rows.check: The final-layer Mess3 belief state is linearly decodable. But the paper says Mess3 next-token distances are preserved, so this single-state result does not show information beyond the next token.

source_check.correct: State: observed for the indirect V2 test. The final-layer representation recovers belief-state geometry; belief states determine future-token distributions. No reported result establishes partial recovery specifically for future tokens.
source_check.problem: The partial state confuses an indirect measure with an empirically incomplete effect.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the Mess3 Process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Measured belief-state geometry representation at multiple points during training

conditions.value: multiple points; specific stages not stated

rows.measure: Emergence of the projected belief-state geometry
rows.value: The simplex structure emerged gradually over training.
rows.note: The paper also says regression errors decreased throughout training, without giving numerical values in the text.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the Mess3 Process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Fit the linear regression on 20% of input-activation pairs and evaluated on the held-out 80%
rows.measure: Belief-state geometry representation and regression mean squared error
rows.value: The held-out geometry remained well represented, and its mean squared error was similar to the full-data regression.
rows.note: The paper reports that the cross-validation procedure was repeated 1000 times; no numerical error or uncertainty is stated in the text.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.1, Figure 6B and Figure 6D; Appendix A.7.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the Mess3 Process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Shuffled the input-to-belief-state correspondences while preserving the overall belief-state geometry
rows.measure: Belief-state geometry recovered by linear regression
rows.value: The projection collapsed the data to the simplex center.
rows.note: This is a control showing that the recovered geometry depends on the correspondence between inputs and their ground-truth belief states.
rows.check: This is a shuffle control. 'Absent' is the expected control outcome, not evidence against V2.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the RRXOR process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Applied linear regression to residual activations from individual layers
rows.measure: Recovery of the ground-truth belief-state geometry
rows.value: The belief-state geometry was not represented in any individual layer.
rows.note: The study reports the result for individual layers collectively, not separate numerical results for each layer.
rows.check: Correct as stated: the RRXOR belief geometry, which carries beyond-next-token information, is not in any individual layer's hidden state.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Linear regression did not recover the full RRXOR belief-state geometry from individual layers. This does not establish that individual hidden states lack information sufficient to predict tokens several positions ahead.
source_check.problem: Absence of linearly recovered belief geometry is stronger evidence about the chosen representation measure than about absence of V2.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the RRXOR process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Applied linear regression to concatenated residual activations from all layers
rows.measure: Recovery of the ground-truth belief-state geometry
rows.baseline: Individual-layer activations, where the geometry was not represented
rows.value: The concatenated activations provided a veridical representation of the belief-state geometry.
rows.note: This is a distributed, multi-layer representation, not a result for a single layer's hidden state.
rows.check: This should link to V2. It shows future-relevant information is present at one position when layers are concatenated, which is a looser reading of 'single hidden state'.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for the single-hidden-state V2 claim. Belief geometry is recovered from concatenated residual activations across all layers at one position.
source_check.problem: The observed representation uses multiple layers and does not establish the result for a single hidden state.

rows.subject: transformer trained on the RRXOR process
rows.stage_stated: trained from scratch on HMM-generated sequences
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise distances in the represented states with distances in ground-truth belief states and next-token probabilities
rows.value: R² = 0.95 for ground-truth belief-state distances; R² = 0.31 for next-token-probability distances.
rows.note: The paper describes the represented geometry as the concatenated-layer representation; the comparison indicates structure beyond next-token predictions alone.
rows.check: This should link to V2. Belief distances fit at R²=0.95 versus 0.31 for next-token distances, using the concatenated-layer representation.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. The concatenated-layer representation has distance correspondence R²=0.95 with belief states and R²=0.31 with next-token probabilities.
source_check.problem: The distance comparison demonstrates structure beyond next-token probabilities across layers, without testing single-state future-token prediction.

relationships.condition: Mess3, final-layer residual stream (synthetic HMM, 4-layer transformer)
relationships.reason: A single final-layer state linearly encodes the belief state, which determines the future-token distribution. It held under cross-validation and emerged with training (R1, R2, R3, with shuffle control R4). Here this is largely next-token-equivalent information.
relationships.display_finding: A single state linearly encoded the belief state determining future-token distributions; recovery held under cross-validation and emerged during training, although the information was largely equivalent to next-token prediction.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Mess3, final-layer residual stream (synthetic HMM, 4-layer transformer)
source_check.reason: R1–R3 recover belief-state information from a single final-layer state, with R4 as a shuffle control. Belief states determine future-token distributions, providing indirect support; V2 does not require information distinct from next-token probabilities.

relationships.condition: RRXOR, where belief states are degenerate in next-token prediction
relationships.reason: Beyond-next-token information is absent from every individual layer and recoverable only from concatenated layers (R5, R6, R7; R²=0.95 vs 0.31).
relationships.display_finding: Individual layers failed to linearly recover full belief geometry, while concatenated layers recovered it with reported R² values of 0.95 versus 0.31.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: RRXOR, where belief states are degenerate in next-token prediction
source_check.reason: R5 tests linear recovery of full belief geometry, not whether a single state contains enough information to predict several tokens ahead. R6–R7 establish a concatenated-layer result. Untested single-state future-token prediction cannot receive limits_scope.

relation.reason: The study reports its own representation experiments bearing indirectly on V2, rather than merely citing or using the finding.

tranche.reason: The synthetic HMM setting supplies an indirect result on future information in hidden states through recovery of belief states that determine future-token distributions.

source_check.notes: Support for V2 is indirect: the study decodes belief states, without measuring future-token decoding at specified horizons. The authors explicitly leave implementation of Bayesian updating untested; their conclusion is accurately paraphrased.

statements.correction: Mess3 final-layer belief geometry recovered by linear regression; 20% regression training and 80% held-out evaluation; emergence during training; shuffle collapse. Appendix A.8 provides code reproduction instructions; public code availability cannot be verified from the supplied text.
statements.problem: The experimental description is correct, but the categorical assertion of no code is unsupported: Appendix A.8 describes provided notebooks, saved models and training scripts.

statements.correction: RRXOR full belief-state geometry not recovered from individual layers; recovered from concatenated layers. Distance correspondence: belief states R²=0.95; next-token probabilities R²=0.31. Single-layer prediction of tokens several positions ahead was not tested.
statements.problem: The geometry findings and R² values are correct. Their classification as a limit on V2 overstates what failure of the individual-layer linear geometry probe establishes.

statements.correction: RRXOR belief-state geometry was linearly recoverable from concatenated layers and not from individual layers. Absence of future information from individual layers was not established.
statements.problem: The multi-layer qualification is correct, but information appearing only in concatenation overstates the finding about linearly recoverable geometry.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Linear regression recovered the ground-truth belief-state geometry from the final residual stream, which the study treats as predictive information beyond local next-token prediction (R1).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that belief-state geometry was absent from every individual layer, although it was present when layer activations were concatenated (R5).
